hints: Start by splitting the ester at the COO link, remember hydrolysis always gives a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol.
Identify your two hydrolysis products here as butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.
Now think about hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$, which oxidises a primary alcohol fully to a carboxylic acid but leaves a carboxylic acid unchanged.
walkthrough:
**Hydrolyse the ester first**

Think of an ester as acid part + alcohol part joined at the $\text{CO}_2$ group. Adding water splits it back apart.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**List the product mixture**

You now have two carbon compounds in the flask. The acid part gives butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and the alcohol part gives ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.

**Apply hot acidified KMnO4**

Hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is a very strong oxidiser. Carboxylic acids resist further oxidation, so butanoic acid survives unchanged. A primary alcohol like ethanol is oxidised in two stages right through to a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2[O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Collect the final carbon products**

So the ethanol becomes ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, while the original butanoic acid remains. The final carbon-containing mixture is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests only propanoic acid remains, which does not match either fragment. The acid fragment has four carbons, not three, and the oxidised ethanol fragment is missing.
options.B: Incorrect. Ethanoic acid from ethanol is correct, but propanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is wrong. The acid from hydrolysis is butanoic acid with one more $\text{CH}_2$ group, and it is not oxidised.
options.C: Correct. Hydrolysis gives butanoic acid plus ethanol. Hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ leaves butanoic acid unchanged but oxidises ethanol fully to ethanoic acid, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.
options.D: Incorrect. This is just the hydrolysis mixture with no oxidation. It forgets that hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ will oxidise the primary alcohol ethanol to ethanoic acid, so ethanol cannot survive.
